# 1.2.99 - one window kit for the module's windows, every window folds, tabs of equal width on one line, one number stepper, notices under the windows in Stained Glass and over them in Monokuma Legacy, the project icon at full opacity, Delete a Remnant on the Investigation dashboard, and a project's description on its token's card

Stage E44 ships alone with this version (the owner, 03.11.2026: the plan's order, E60 as 1.2.98, then E44 as 1.2.99).
It was planned as one set of windows before E21: the mockups the owner approved, a window kit (`scripts/ui-kit.mjs`,
`styles/components.css`), a CSS contract with its tools, and fixes to `live.mjs`. What E44 ships: the CSS lint, its
budget, a contrast check and the computed-style sweep (C1); `live.mjs` that loses no press and keeps a raised window up
(C2); the kit (C3); one tab system, one number stepper, no window's collapse blocked and a word in every empty choice
(C4); the notice history (C5) and the room, voice and launcher tiles (C6) on the kit with their look unchanged; the
approved mockups recorded (C7); then the owner's additions of 04.11.2026 - the project icon at full opacity, notices by
theme and Delete a Remnant on the Investigation dashboard (C8), and a project's required description on its token's
card (C9); then a fix round, FG1 to FG6. **This version adds no setting, no GM store, no socket, no bridge row and no
migration; it changes what GMs and players see in many windows, and a project now needs a description** (Before
installing). Nothing in this version has been run at a real table or in Foundry; what was measured was measured
headless, and the look in Chromium through the style sweep and the glass sweep; the gaps are listed in Known gaps and
Checked. 29 commits on top of 1.2.98 (main c4210b4d, the 1.2.98 release and its local-gate record), up to 4dac4f1d, the
last code commit; no merges.

## Before installing

1. **Back up the world, and note the version you ran,** so a problem can be traced back.
2. **Nothing to switch in another module.** The dimmed tokens on a player's screen reported on 1.2.98 come from two
   settings outside the module (Isometric Perspective's *Enable Occlusion: Dynamic Tile*, and the scene's darkness while
   its global light is not bright); the GM handbook names both, and the module changes neither.
3. **What changes in a running world.**
   - **No setting is added, removed or renamed.** `scripts/settings.mjs` does not change.
   - **A project's description** (C9, FG1, FG3, FG6), at most 1000 characters, stored by its project's secrecy:
     - a public project's in the world setting `projectMeta`, as a new field `description` beside the room - world data
       on every browser, as the project's name in Daggerheart's Countdowns already is;
     - a secret project's in the GMs' store `projectSecrets` (the existing store; no GM store is added), with
       `descriptionTold`, which player was told which words; it moves between the two halves when the project is
       revealed or made secret again; `world-secrets.mjs` gains a rule that holds it out of a secret project's row of
       `projectMeta` alone.
     - A description past 1000 characters is refused on every road, never cut: at the field, in `createProject` and
       `updateProject`, and in a `project.change` from another GM (`cleanProjectChange`). A player writes it once, in the
       proposal; after creation only the GMs change it.
     - A project made before 1.2.99 has none; its card draws none, and its edit window asks for one when a GM opens it.
       The Projects tab's table Save never refuses a project for lacking one.
   - **No migration.** No stored data is rewritten and no flag or setting is renamed.
   - **Bridge rows and sockets: no new bridge row, no new socket listener, no new sync kind.** `bridge-wire.mjs`,
     `bridge-table.mjs`, `bridge-guards.mjs`, `sync.mjs` and `migrate.mjs` do not change. The players in on a secret
     project read its description from a private chat card the primary GM whispers to them, veiled, by the road the
     proposer of a public project is already told by; the card of a public project reads `projectMeta`.
   - **The language files** gain 24 keys in each language and lose 3 (`DRPG.Assign.title`, `DRPG.Despair.poolsTitle`,
     `DRPG.Monokuma.panelTitle`, whose only readers were Despair Flow's tabs); one text changes (`DRPG.Remnant.tieOpen`,
     "-" before, now "- not decided -").
   - **For macros and other modules:** `tools/api-surface.json` gains one row, `styleSnapshot` (`game.drpg.styleSnapshot()`,
     the computed style of the module's surfaces). `game.drpg.openNotices()` answers "raised" instead of the window when
     the notice history is already open.
   - **What a GM and a player see differently.**
     - **Every window folds** (C4b, FG2): a double-click on a window's title bar folds it to the bar and a second one
       opens it again - on the module's windows, the character sheets and other modules' windows; until 1.2.99 the
       module blocked the gesture on every window (`scripts/no-collapse.mjs` is removed). A short window that asks one
       question, such as a confirmation, does not fold, as Foundry's own do not. A tile or launcher pressed while its
       window is folded opens it and brings it to the front; a messenger window folded to its bar does not mark a
       message read until it is opened again.
     - **Tabs** (C4a): the ten tabbed windows share one tab bar; the tabs of a bar have equal widths and stand on one
       line, with a smaller font down to an 11 px floor where needed; a bar that does not fit even then goes to rows
       (the window grows by at most 25 % only once E21 puts it on the kit's frame). Despair Flow's tabs read **Pools**,
       **Monokumas**, **Students**, **Overflow** (PL *Pule*, *Monokumy*, *Uczniowie*, *Overflow*). Item tables' pool
       names wrap, and its layout follows the window.
     - **One number stepper** (C4b): the twelve number fields (Edit campaign, Season setup, Despair Flow's Overflow and
       others) are a field with - and + buttons in both themes, the first time Monokuma Legacy has one; their names,
       ranges and readers do not change.
     - **A word in every empty choice** (C4b): no list offers a bare "-"; the empty choice reads "- nobody -", "- no
       Remnant -", "- pick a statistic -", "- no project -", "- no room -" or "- not set -".
     - **The notice history** (C5): one scrolling list, **Clear** on the left and **Close** on the right; under Stained
       Glass its small type is at the glass's text floor (21 px; 13 and 14.95 px before), kept so by the owner for 1.2.99.
     - **Notices by theme** (C8c): under **Stained Glass** the notice cards stand under every window, so a window dragged
       over them covers them; under **Monokuma Legacy** every card stands over the windows. The split by kind of 1.2.98
       (a whisper under, a card to the table over) is gone.
     - **The project icon at full opacity** (C8b): a project's token is drawn at full opacity (0.7 before) on every
       screen, and a token placed before is brought up to it; its colour is unchanged (amber while built, green when
       done).
     - **Delete a Remnant** (C8d): the Investigation dashboard's **Remnants** tab has a **Delete** on each row, for a GM.
       It asks first, naming the Remnant ("Its token goes from the map and its row from the case."), then removes the
       token and the case's row together; a reinforced Remnant is refused with its notice.
     - **A project's Description** (C9, FG1): the player's proposal and the GM's create and edit windows have a required
       **Description**; an empty one, or one past 1000 characters, is refused with words under the field and the window
       stays open with the text. Choosing a project of a set kind (Secret Passage, Breach the Wall, Seal the passage,
       Close the breach, Repair an item) writes the kind's name in the field, editable, and names no room or item. The GM
       reads the player's text on approval and may change it. Everyone who knows the project reads it on the project
       token's card, under the bar, and an open card follows a GM's edit.
     - The room, voice and launcher tiles, "Who you hear", the GM's hexagon and Foundry tools' launcher and frames are
       built by the kit with their look unchanged (C6).
   - `module.json` still reads version 1.2.98; the release commit sets the version. It serves one new stylesheet,
     `styles/components.css`, before `narrow.css`.
   - **The package.** `git archive` lists 249 entries at c4210b4d and 252 at 4dac4f1d: `scripts/ui-kit.mjs`,
     `scripts/style-snapshot.mjs`, `scripts/tests-css.mjs` and `styles/components.css` added, `scripts/no-collapse.mjs`
     removed; `scripts/` holds 197 module files (195 before). 183 files change (+15074, -2896), 94 added, one removed;
     the 54 approved pictures under `audit/design/` and the 27 window captures under `audit/windows/` are not in the
     package.
   - **The stage ledger** (`tools/stages.json`, FG4): E44 `touches` ["scenes", "sockets"]; one new row, E92 (Spectator),
     `planned` 1.2.108, right before E72, as the owner placed it; the 24 rows from E72 to E58 one release later each
     (E72 1.2.109 ... E58 1.2.131; E61 and E62 1.2.110), E26 still 1.3.0; 89 rows, 53 shipped (88 and 53 before). No
     drill is named.
